_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, docs, reference data, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data: rows that look like real records, whose real version is
sitting right there in the operator's life and is structurally indistinguishable.
Must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py -- a real record cannot be regenerated,
so pasting one in fails at commit. (A self-evidently fake canary or an Acme mock is
NOT lifelike and does not need a generator; the risk it guards against is a person
reaching for a convenient REAL example, and there is no temptation to reach for a
real value that would look obviously wrong next to FAKE_CANARY_XYZ.)
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never git-tracked. Lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. This repo ships only the schema.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
_audited: 2026-07-31 RE-AUDIT (supersedes the 2026-07-16 sweep). The earlier sweep asked only whether shipped code appends to a TRACKED file here. That question is too narrow: it clears every path that is gitignored, and .gitignore is advisory -- `git add -f` walks straight through it, which is the whole reason declarations exist. This pass asked instead whether shipped code or shipped docs can put REAL-RUN OUTPUT at a repo-relative path at all. ANSWER: it produces real-run output -- the reminder DB itself, plus the two-way bus cursors, inboxes and tick log -- and none of it is repo-relative. store.py resolves the DB from the SCHEDULE_DB_PATH env var, else a per-user directory under the home dir; ingest.py, dispatch.py, digest.py and relay.py all write under the Agent Center state dir, also outside this repo. The db.sqlite3 and config.json lines in this repo's .gitignore are defensive: no shipped code writes either name here. Nothing to declare, and that is a conclusion, not a default.
_armed: 2026-07-31 ARMED. The empty declaration above stopped being the control on this date. An independent verifier cloned this repo, committed metrics/live-runs.jsonl and runs/transcript.json into it, and tools/data_boundary.py exited 0: checks 1..3 only ever inspect what the manifest DECLARES, so a manifest that declares nothing was enforcing nothing, and the careful paragraph above was doing the work a check is supposed to do. Check 4 now runs off the TRACKED FILE LIST instead and fails any file wearing the shape of real-run output (a jsonl under metrics/, a runs/ tree, a dated file under an output dir, a live-ledger filename, a database) whether or not this manifest declares a thing. So the empty `data` list is a claim re-tested on every commit and in CI, not a note taken on faith. That distinction is load-bearing here: store.py takes the DB path from $SCHEDULE_DB_PATH before falling back to a per-user directory, so 'the default resolver points elsewhere' was never the same statement as 'nothing can land here'.
_data_home: $SCHEDULE_REMINDER_DATA_DIR -- a private dir OUTSIDE this repo. If this skill ever needs to record real-run output, it goes THERE -- never back into this repo.
